M. Rossabi, Khubilai Khan (1988); The Cambridge History of Japan vol. 3 (1990): the Kamakura bakufu under Hōjō Sadatoki

G. Coedès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (1968): Singhasari under Kertanegara, Dharmasraya after the Pamalayu expedition (1275), Sukhothai, Lan Na, Champa, Angkor

K. W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (2013): Trần Nhân Tông

M. E. Smith, The Aztecs (3rd ed., 2012): the Valley of Mexico before Tenochtitlan (1325)
B. Bauer, Ancient Cuzco (2004); M. Moseley, The Incas and their Ancestors (2001): Chimor
notes: Date: 1 January 1291. Kublai Khan rules all of China after the fall of the Song (1279); Goryeo and the Sakya hierarchs of Tibet are under the Yuan; Qaidu and Du'a hold Central Asia (south_east.py).

India: Jalal al-Din Khalji has ruled Delhi since June 1290; Bengal (Lakhnauti) is under Balban's son Bughra Khan and his son Kaykaus. The Deccan kingdoms (Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas, Pandyas) are still independent; Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis (both 1340s) did not exist yet.
Sri Lanka: after the Pandya sack of Yapahuwa (1284) the Sinhalese kingdom is weak; its ruler between 1284 and 1302 is uncertain (gap).
Java: Singhasari under Kertanegara (Majapahit is founded only in 1293). Pagan's empire broke apart after the Mongol invasion (1287); Pagan itself survives under Kyawswa, Martaban under Wareru (1287).

Ayutthaya (1351), Lan Xang (1353), Singapura (c.1299), the Red Turban states, the Ashikaga and the Southern Court of 1356 are left out; Tenochtitlan (1325) and the Purépecha state (c.1320s) did not exist yet.
Rulers of the Americas are not known by name for 1291; Cahokia is in decline but still occupied.

states.dynasty_note: Kublai Khan, Great Khan and Emperor Shizu of Yuan (1260-94). The crown prince Zhenjin died in 1286; his son Temür succeeds in 1294.

summary.en: The old Kublai rules all of China; his campaigns against Japan, Vietnam and Java have failed or are being prepared.
summary.de: Der greise Kublai beherrscht ganz China; seine Feldzüge gegen Japan, Vietnam und Java sind gescheitert oder in Vorbereitung.

states.dynasty_note: King Chungnyeol, son-in-law of Kublai; Goryeo is a Yuan vassal.
Emperor Fushimi reigns in Kyoto; power lies with the Kamakura bakufu, the shogun prince Hisaaki and the regent Hōjō Sadatoki. Kyushu is guarded against a third Mongol invasion.

ruler.name: Sakya hierarchs and dpon-chen under the Yuan

states.dynasty_note: Tibet is governed for the Yuan by the Sakya school and its administrators (dpon-chen); the Drikung rising was crushed in 1290.
The Khalji took the throne in June 1290 after the last Mamluk (Slave) sultan. The Mongols of the Chagatai raid the Punjab.
Balban's son Bughra Khan rules Bengal as an independent sultan; his son Kaykaus succeeds c.1291.
The Soomra dynasty of lower Sindh (Ismaili tradition).
Hindu kings of Kashmir (the sultanate dates from 1339); names around 1290 uncertain.
Vaghela king of Gujarat (1275-96); conquered by the Khalji in 1299.
The declining Paramara kingdom, divided between rival claimants.
Hammira repulses Jalal al-Din's attacks (1290-92).
Ramachandra (1271-1311), raided by Ala al-Din Khalji in 1296.
Prataparudra succeeded his grandmother Rudramadevi (d. c.1289).
At the height of the later Pandyas (1268-1310); Marco Polo visits the coast in 1292. Venad and the Kerala coast are attached through the spread.
Pandya armies sacked Yapahuwa (1284) and took the Tooth Relic; the throne is uncertain until Parakramabahu III (1302).
Aryacakravarti kings, vassals of the Pandya.
Victor over the third Mongol invasion (Bạch Đằng, 1288).
Che Man, king from 1288.
Angkor under Jayavarman VIII (1243-95), paying tribute to Kublai since 1285. Lavo (Lopburi) is in its sphere.
Ram Khamhaeng (c.1279-98) has extended his overlordship to the Malay peninsula (Nakhon Si Thammarat).
Mangrai took Hariphunchai (Lamphun) in 1281/92; Chiang Mai is founded only in 1296.
The remnant of the Pagan empire after the Mongol invasion (1287); the three Myinsaing brothers hold Kyaukse.
Wareru proclaimed himself king at Martaban in 1287 (Pegu taken c.1287-96).
Kertanegara (1268-92), who sent the Pamalayu expedition to Sumatra (1275) and mutilated Kublai's envoys (1289); Majapahit rises from his fall (1292-93).
Melayu at Dharmasraya, heir to Srivijaya, under Singhasari overlordship since the Pamalayu expedition.
The first Muslim ruler on Sumatra (d. 1297); Marco Polo calls at Samudra in 1292.
The Tepanec of Azcapotzalco, a rising lordship (its hegemony comes in the 14th century).
The great Mississippian centre, past its peak and losing people; abandoned by c.1350.
The early Inca kingdom of Cusco, one of several Andean chiefdoms (rulers before Pachacuti are legendary).
